    "design": "# QC Release Gate — Implementable Design\n\nRepo root: `E:/lims-migration/durdans-lims` (monorepo; the `E:/2nd year project/durdans-lims` tree is the pre-consolidation copy — do not edit it).\n\n---\n\n## 1. The invariant\n\n> **No patient result may be technically verified or clinically authorized unless the internal QC governing its analyser and analyte at the time of measurement passed — or a lab supervisor has explicitly released it over a failed control, with a recorded reason.**\n\nTwo clinician-facing corollaries that make it testable: a result whose QC is *unknown* is held, not released; and a result released over a failed control still reads **FAIL** everywhere it appears, never **PASS**.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Linkage decision\n\n### 2.1 The three broken dimensions and the ruling on each\n\n| Dimension | Today | Ruling |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Instrument** | 3 vocabularies: `qc_result.instrument` display names, `instruments.json` `inst-00N`, listener constant `ASTM-IN-01`. No registry table. | Create a real `instrument` table with `code` as the single canonical id. All three producers switch to it. **`qc_result` is empty in production** (nothing calls `POST /qc-runs`), so the existing `instrument` column is *reused* as the canonical code — no backfill, no second column. |\n| **Analyte** | `qc_result.analyte` free text at *panel* granularity; results keyed via `parameter_id → test_parameters.loinc_code`. | Add `qc_result.loinc_code`. QC is recorded **per analyte, per control level** — one row per LOINC — which is what Westgard actually is. The panel-name seed JSON stays demo data and is no longer served (§2.4). `analyte` survives as the human label only. |\n| **Time** | No measurement timestamp on `test_results`; `created_at` is `timestamp` (no tz), and is *stale on re-ingest* because line 77-79 reuses the existing row. | Add `test_results.measured_at timestamptz`, set at every write path. Never join on `created_at`. |\n\n### 2.2 Governing-QC rule (the definition of \"same run\")\n\n> For a result with `instrument_code = I`, parameter LOINC `L`, `measured_at = T`:\n> for **each distinct `control_level`** on (I, L), take the most recent `qc_result` with `performed_at <= T`. The result's QC state is the **worst** of those per-level states. If the newest of them is older than `T − app.qc.max-age-hours` (default 24) the state is `STALE`. If none exists, `NO_QC`.\n\nJudgement calls, one line each:\n- **Time-bracketed, not run-id.** No analytical-run id exists on the wire (`AstmMessage.parse` reads only R fields 2/3/4/6) and inventing one forces QC operators to type an id they never see. Latest-at-or-before is the standard fallback and needs zero workflow change.\n- **`T` is `measured_at`, not `now()`.** A result sitting three days in the verify queue must not become STALE by ageing; staleness is a property of the run.\n- **WARN does not hold.** 1-2s is a warning rule by construction (`WestgardEvaluator` line ~48 does not set `rejected`); holding on it would generate constant false holds and the gate would be switched off within a week.\n- **Branch scoping is free.** Each `instrument.code` belongs to exactly one branch, so keying on instrument code alone also closes the cross-branch Westgard-series leak in `QcService` without a branch parameter.\n\n### 2.3 Liquibase — two additive changesets\n\n**File 1** — `apps/lims-core-service/lims-core-service-app/src/main/resources/liquibase/changelog/20260801120000_create_instrument_registry.xml`\n\n```xml\n<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n<databaseChangeLog\n        xmlns=\"http://www.liquibase.org/xml/ns/dbchangelog\"\n        xmlns:xsi=\"http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance\"\n        xsi:schemaLocation=\"http://www.liquibase.org/xml/ns/dbchangelog\n        http://www.liquibase.org/xml/ns/dbchangelog/dbchangelog-3.8.xsd\">\n\n    <!-- WHY: 'instrument' exists in three unreconciled identifier spaces (display\n         names in qc_result, inst-00N in instruments.json, ASTM-IN-01 in the TCP\n         listener). Validation is enforced in `QcService.record` instead (§3, step 3).\n\n**File 2** — `.../changelog/20260801121000_add_test_result_qc_linkage.xml`\n\n```xml\n<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n<databaseChangeLog\n        xmlns=\"http://www.liquibase.org/xml/ns/dbchangelog\"\n        xmlns:xsi=\"http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance\"\n        xsi:schemaLocation=\"http://www.liquibase.org/xml/ns/dbchangelog\n        http://www.liquibase.org/xml/ns/dbchangelog/dbchangelog-3.8.xsd\">\n\n    <!-- WHY: test_results has no instrument and no measurement timestamp, so\n         \"which QC governed this result\" is inexpressible. PASS|WARN|FAIL|STALE|NO_QC|NOT_REQUIRED|NOT_EVALUATED -->\n            <column name=\"qc_status\" type=\"varchar(16)\"/>\n            <!-- The exact qc_result row consulted: \"show me the QC that governed\n                 this result\" becomes a single lookup, not an inference. -->\n            <column name=\"qc_result_id\" type=\"uuid\"/>\n            <column name=\"qc_override_by\" type=\"varchar(255)\"/>\n            <column name=\"qc_override_at\" type=\"timestamp with time zone\"/>\n            <column name=\"qc_override_reason\" type=\"varchar(500)\"/>\n        </addColumn>\n    </changeSet>\n\n    <!-- Make the legacy state explicit rather than NULL, so \"never evaluated\"\n         is distinguishable from \"column not yet written\". -->\n    <changeSet id=\"20260801121000-2-backfill-not-evaluated\" author=\"lims\">\n        <update tableName=\"test_results\">\n            <column name=\"qc_status\" value=\"NOT_EVALUATED\"/>\n            <where>qc_status IS NULL</where>\n        </update>\n    </changeSet>\n\n    <changeSet id=\"20260801121000-3-qc-index\" author=\"lims\">\n        <createIndex tableName=\"test_results\" indexName=\"idx_test_results_qc\">\n            <column name=\"instrument_code\"/>\n            <column name=\"measured_at\"/>\n        </createIndex>\n    </changeSet>\n</databaseChangeLog>\n```\n\nAppend both `<include>` lines to `master.xml` after `20260801100000_add_critical_values_nav.xml`.\n\n### 2.4 Default for unlinked data — and why it is not a date cutoff\n\n**The gate keys off the presence of `instrument_code`, not off a date.**\n\n- `instrument_code IS NULL` → `qc_status = NOT_EVALUATED` → **does not hold**. Absence of linkage is not evidence of QC failure; blocking the back catalogue would be a lab outage on deploy day.\n- Every one of the three write paths sets `instrument_code` from day one (§3), so *no new result can be NULL*. There is no clock, no cutoff, and no window in which a new result silently escapes.\n- The one legitimate NULL-equivalent is `BENCH-MANUAL` (`qc_required = false`) → `NOT_REQUIRED`. That is an auditable choice made by a named MLT, not a silent gap.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Hook points, in implementation order\n\n**0. Behaviour matrix\n\n`measured_at = T`. \"Hold\" = result stays `ENTERED`, sample `SENT_FOR_VERIFICATION`.\n\n| QC state at T | Autoverify (`ingest`) | Manual entry (`processResults`) | Verify (`verifyResult` / `bulkVerify`) | Authorize (`authorizeResult`) |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **PASS** — governing controls all PASS within 24 h | Normal flag → auto-release `TECHNICALLY_VERIFIED`/`AUTO-VERIFY`; abnormal still held by the existing flag rules | Stamp `PASS`; land `ENTERED` | Verify proceeds | Authorize proceeds |\n| **WARN** — 1-2s only | Auto-release; `qc_status=WARN` shown amber in the supervisor grid | Stamp `WARN` | Verify proceeds (WARN is advisory) | Proceeds |\n| **FAIL** — 1-3s/2-2s/R-4s/4-1s/10x rejected | **Hold**, reason `QC FAIL for <LOINC>` | Stamp `FAIL`; land `ENTERED` (entry never blocked) | **Blocked** — 422 naming the parameters. Supervisor may override (§5). Bulk reports `FAILED: QC hold: …` | **Blocked** unless an override stamp is present; pathologist cannot create one |\n| **STALE** — newest control older than `T − 24 h` | **Hold** | Stamp `STALE` | **Blocked**; override allowed | **Blocked** without override |\n| **NO_QC** — no control ever recorded for (instrument, LOINC) | **Hold** | Stamp `NO_QC` | **Blocked**; override allowed | **Blocked** without override |\n| **NOT_REQUIRED** — `instrument.qc_required = false` (e.g. `BENCH-MANUAL`) | n/a (instrument path always has an analyser) | Stamp `NOT_REQUIRED` | Proceeds | Proceeds |\n| **NOT_EVALUATED** — `instrument_code` NULL (pre-change rows only) | n/a | n/a | Proceeds | Proceeds |\n\n**Operational cost of fail-closed, stated plainly.** On the day the gate ships, every analyte for which no QC has been recorded becomes `NO_QC` and every instrument result is held. That is a real workload spike, and it is the point: it makes visible that QC is not being run. Mitigations: (a) `app.qc.max-age-hours` is configurable, (b) `POST /api/v1/mlt/qc-runs` already exists and only needs a frontend form to make the holds clearable, (c) supervisors have a documented override. Deploy with the QC-entry form, not before it.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Override\n\n- **Who:** `LAB_SUPERVISOR`, `BRANCH_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN` (checked with `SecurityUtils.hasRole`). **MLT cannot override** — an MLT who ran the failing control must not be the one who waives it. `PATHOLOGIST` cannot create one either (§3 step 10).\n- **Where:** only inside `VerificationService.verifyResult`. One code path, no second entry point — matching the class's own stated design for `findResultById`.\n- **What is required:** `VerificationRequest` gains `String qcOverrideReason`. Non-blank and ≥ 20 characters, else `BusinessRuleException(\"A QC override requires a documented reason (min 20 characters).\")`. No default, no reason picked from a dropdown of one.\n- **What is recorded, per released result:** `qc_override_by` (username), `qc_override_at`, `qc_override_reason`, plus the unchanged `qc_status` (still `FAIL`) and `qc_result_id` pointing at the exact control that failed.\n- **Audit:** one row via the existing `auditService.log(...)` (`@Transactional(MANDATORY)` — `verifyResult` is transactional, so it joins the same commit) with action `QC_OVERRIDE_RELEASE`, entity type `TEST_RESULT`, entity id = result id, patient code from `sample.getOrderItem().getOrder().getPatientId()`, details = `{instrumentCode, loinc, qcState, governingQcId, reason}`. The audit log is already tamper-evident (`20260619120000_tamper_evident_audit_log.xml` BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers), so the override chain is hash-linked.\n- **What the override does NOT do:** it does not change `qc_status` to `PASS`. The supervisor grid, the pathologist queue and `TestResultDetailResponse` continue to show `FAIL`. Laundering a failed control into a passing status is the exact failure mode the gate exists to prevent.\n\n---\n\n## 6. multi-level worst-status wins; `STALE` computed against `measured_at` not `now()`; unknown instrument → `NOT_REQUIRED`; null instrument → `NOT_EVALUATED`; different instrument code → `NO_QC` (proves the join is instrument-scoped, i.e. a chemistry failure cannot hold haematology).\n2. **`qc/QcServiceRecordTest`** (integration) — the currently untested write path: PASS/WARN/FAIL derivation including the untested `4-1s` and the `WARN` branch at `QcService:63`; unknown instrument code rejected; blank `loincCode` rejected; series is per-`(instrument, loinc, level)`.\n3. **`qc/QcHoldIngestionIntegrationTest`**: failing control → result `ENTERED`, sample `SENT_FOR_VERIFICATION`, `qc_status = \"FAIL\"`, `qc_result_id` = the failing row's id; passing control → auto-release; stale control → hold; no control → hold; `instrument_code` NULL (legacy row seeded directly) → releases with `NOT_EVALUATED`.\n4. **`qc/QcGateVerificationIntegrationTest`** — the invariant test: `verifyResult` on a `FAIL` result throws and the result stays `ENTERED`; **`bulkVerify` with that id returns `FAILED: QC hold…` and the sample is not `VERIFIED`** (this is the named bypass, and it must be a test, not an inference); override by `LAB_SUPERVISOR` with a 20-char reason succeeds, stamps `qc_override_by/at/reason`, leaves `qc_status = \"FAIL\"`, and writes a `QC_OVERRIDE_RELEASE` audit row; override attempted by `MLT` is rejected; override with a blank reason is rejected.\n5. **`qc/QcGateAuthorizationIntegrationTest`**: a `TECHNICALLY_VERIFIED` result carrying `qc_status = FAIL` and no override (constructible only by seeding, i.e. a defence-in-depth case) is refused at `authorizeResult`; with an override stamp it authorizes and dispatch registration proceeds.\n6. **`mapper/TestResultMapperTest`**: `toSummaryResponse` returns the entity's `qcStatus`, and `NOT_EVALUATED` for null — pins the literal so it cannot regress.\n\nExpected suite after this work: 141 → ~171 (6 new classes, ~30 methods; 2 existing methods keep their assertions and gain fixture rows).\n\n---\n\n## 7. What this deliberately does NOT do\n\nEach of these was considered and cut, with the reason.\n\n1. **No analytical run id.** `AstmMessage.parse` reads only O and R records, fields 2/3/4/6; there is no run/batch field on the wire, and synthesising one would force QC operators to record an id they never see. Time-bracketing is an *inference* where an explicit run linkage would be a *record* — an ISO 15189 assessor would prefer the latter. Named as the top follow-up.\n2. **No bracketing QC.** Only the control *before* `T` governs. A control run *after* the specimen that fails does not retroactively hold it. Real practice brackets both sides; doing so requires a look-back queue and a result-recall workflow.\n3. **No retro-hold / look-back of already-released or dispatched results.** When a QC failure lands, results released earlier under a then-passing control are not revisited. This needs a recall + corrected-report workflow, and `ResultStatus.DISPATCHED` is never assigned anywhere in `main`, so `ResultAmendmentService`'s `CORRECTED_REPORT_REQUIRED` branch (line 156) is currently unreachable — that defect must be fixed first.\n4. **No per-result instrument id from the analyser.** The simulator transmits it in ASTM R field 12 and a measurement timestamp in field 11 (`Lis2Records:62-71`); `AstmMessage.Result` has no slot for either. `measured_at` is therefore ingestion time, and `instrument_code` is per-listener config. Accurate to within seconds for a live analyser; wrong for a replayed batch. Adding R-11/R-12 to the parser is a small, isolated follow-up.\n5. **No per-analyte or per-instrument rule sets (IQCP).** `WestgardEvaluator` stays a static final utility with a fixed 6-rule set. Making it an injectable bean with a configurable rule set is correct and cheap, but nothing in this design needs it, and changing it would touch the 5 passing evaluator tests for no invariant gain.\n6. **No multi-level canonical R-4s.** R-4s remains within-level across-time rather than within-run across-materials, and `2of3-2s`, `3-1s`, `6x/7T/8x/9x` remain unimplemented. The gate consumes whatever verdict the evaluator produces; upgrading the rule set is orthogonal.\n7. **No QC lot / reagent-lot / calibration linkage, no control expiry, no Levey-Jennings charts, no QC scheduling or reminders.** `control_lot` remains written-and-never-read. These are a QC *module*; this is a QC *gate*.\n8. **No instrument admin UI.** The `instrument` table is created and seeded by Liquibase only. `instruments.json` remains the source for the read-only instruments screen until someone needs to add a fifth analyser.\n9. **Per-attempt provenance is not modelled.** `uk_test_results_sample_parameter` means one row per (sample, parameter) updated in place, so a re-run on a different analyser overwrites `instrument_code`/`measured_at`. Per-attempt history would be a child table — a materially larger change than three nullable columns, and not needed to make the invariant real.\n10. **`qc_result` is still not soft-deletable or audited** (it does not extend `BaseEntity`). Out of scope, but noted: the gate's evidence table is less protected than `audit_log`, which has tamper-evidence triggers.\n\n**Adjacent live defects this design touches but does not fix** — raise separately before the review: `bulkVerify` still ignores `isSafeForBulkApproval`, so **critical and abnormal results remain bulk-releasable** whenever QC passes (the QC gate covers them only incidentally); `verifyResult` is sample-wide from one anchor id with no flag check; `DispatchService.registerAuthorizedReportSystem` is a public bean method that skips its authorization assertion; `outbox_event` retains patient email/phone past the PDPA erasure window.",
